docs.task: How sessions, events, executions, and messages are stored in the workspace db, and how a session is deleted today.

asks: Explain how sessions, events, executions, and messages are stored in the workspace db.
Explain how a session is deleted today.

data_flow.step: Engine::create_session creates `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<id>/` (plus uploads claimed from staging, a `.gitignore` of `*` in sessions/, and one subfolder per project), then inserts the sessions row with status running, lane research, stage_label Intake.
The engine registers a Live { state, wake, inflight, driving } in the in-memory `sessions` map and appends SessionCreated through Inner::append.

Inner::append: under the per-session state lock, WorkspaceDb::append_event runs one transaction that takes next_seq (MAX(seq)+1 for the session), inserts into events(session_id, seq, type, payload JSON, at), and touches sessions.updated_at.

materialize upserts gates on GateOpened, answers them on GateAnswered, inserts decisions on DecisionMade. Then the fold runs and update_session rewrites status, lane, stage_label, projects, yolo, cost_usd, title on the sessions row. The sessions INSERT and UPDATE OF title, request triggers keep the kind='session' row in search_docs in step.

When an execution spawns, insert_execution writes executions(id, session_id, agent, purpose, stage, project, executor, model, params, spawn_block, report_path, status running, usage, started_at). session_id is NULL for side-panel executions. finish_execution sets status, usage, cost_usd, error, submit, final_text, ended_at.

While a native execution runs, record_message appends each model turn to messages(execution_id, seq, role, content JSON), and the delta stream is appended to activity(execution_id, seq, delta JSON, at). Both use next_seq in a transaction. messages and activity link to a session only through executions.session_id.
Harness executions also write files under `<session>/.state/harness/<execution>/` (hook config, MCP registration, terminal.log), outside the db.

When the fold first reports a terminal state, Inner::append calls remove_session_cache, which deletes `~/.cache/ostra/sandbox/session-<id>` on a thread. On server start, sweep_session_caches repeats this for every Completed or Failed session in every attached workspace.

Deletion today: DELETE /api/workspaces/{id} calls App::delete_workspace, which retires the runtime (refused with a Busy error while a session is Running, Waiting, or Paused or an execution runs), then ostra_workspace::unregister removes the registry row and push subscriptions in one transaction and removes workspace.toml, workspace.db, and its -wal and -shm files. Session folders under .ostra/sessions/ and per-project .ostra/ files stay on disk. No code deletes one session.

patterns.description: Each table has a pub(crate) struct wrapping &Connection in its own module with the SQL. WorkspaceDb has one thin method per call and uses `db.run` (autocommit) or `db.transaction` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, commit or roll back). Anything that deletes across several tables belongs in `db.transaction`, as registry's remove_workspace does.
patterns.name: Repository per table, WorkspaceDb picks the transaction

patterns.description: Inner::append is the single writer: store event, materialize gates and decisions, fold, update the sessions row, remove the sandbox cache when the session first becomes terminal, then broadcast. executions, messages, activity, and tool_calls are written directly by the executor path rather than from events. A restart rebuilds SessionState from `events` alone (Inner::load, Engine::recover).
patterns.name: Event log is the source of truth, other tables are derived

patterns.description: Workspace delete and project removal check for sessions with status Running, Waiting, or Paused and for running executions, return a Busy error whose text names the session and says what to do. Artifact delete follows Rule W4 (no delete while a session has not ended). Stalled sessions are not counted as live by busy().
patterns.name: Delete refuses while a session is live

document.problem: A retention feature needs to know which rows and files belong to a session and what removes them. The workspace db has no session delete: no SQL DELETE touches sessions, events, executions, messages, activity, gates, decisions, tool_calls, or search_docs. The only removals of session data are deleting the whole workspace (db file and toml) and removing the sandbox tool cache of an ended session.
document.scope: Task: how sessions, events, executions, and messages are stored in the workspace db, and how a session is deleted today. Covers the SQLite schema and repositories in ostra-store, the writers in ostra-engine, the on-disk session folder, and every deletion path found. It does not design a retention feature, does not cover the web UI, and does not cover the registry db or project memory db.
document.title: Session storage in the workspace db and how a session is deleted today

submit.findings_summary: The workspace db (`.ostra/workspace.db`, 3 migrations in schema.rs) holds an append-only `events` log keyed (session_id, seq) as the source of truth. Beside it are derived tables: sessions, gates, decisions, search_docs with FTS5 triggers, and executions, with messages, activity, and tool_calls hanging off executions by execution_id. No table declares foreign keys or ON DELETE, so nothing cascades, and messages, activity, and tool_calls reach a session only through executions.session_id. Nothing deletes a single session today: no DELETE route exists for sessions, no store method deletes session rows, and the only per-session removal is the sandbox tool cache. Workspace delete removes workspace.db and workspace.toml after refusing while a session is Running, Waiting, or Paused. The `.ostra/sessions/<id>` folders stay on disk. Spend queries read executions directly, and the engine keeps an in-memory Live map with no removal path.

The registry db, project memory db, and lessons that originate from a session
Cleanup of uploads, harness native session files, and per-project reports outside the session folder
In-memory per-session caches in the server (nav, hub, file touches) that would need to forget a deleted session
docs/ pages describing the workspace db and workspace delete, which a change would need to update
Disk shrinkage after row deletion: WorkspaceDb never runs VACUUM or a WAL checkpoint (only the registry does)

docs.task: How the server starts a workspace and how the CLI commands are defined.

asks: How the server starts a workspace
How the CLI commands are defined

data_flow.step: Process starts. If argv[1] is sandbox-init, hand off to ostra_sandbox::init::main and exit (hidden from help). Otherwise scrub_startup_env, set_helper(current_exe), Cli::parse(), extend_path(), and build a multi-thread tokio runtime.
Match on cli.command. None uses the flattened cli.serve; Some(Serve(args)) uses its own args. Both call runtime.block_on(serve(args)).

serve initializes tracing (OSTRA_LOG filter, default info; writes to stdout and appends to <data_dir>/server.log), converts ServeArgs to ServeOptions (open_browser = !no_open, exe = current_exe), and calls app::run.

run loads the global config (defaults on failure), resolves the bind address (flag, else server.bind, else 127.0.0.1; accepts localhost, all, *), and binds a listener. An explicit port (flag or server.port) binds exactly; otherwise it tries 7878 through 7897, then port 0.
If server.json names no live process, run kills sandbox leftovers and removes stale egress sockets and decoys, then spawns the decoy report watcher on a blocking thread.

build(&opts, port): validate and load the global config and sandbox status (warn when unsandboxed); ensure the data dir; start price refresh; master_key::unlock(open_registry()?); materialize embedded assets into <data_dir>/assets; construct Providers, McpGateway, Management, Coordination, NativeExecutor, Notifier (VAPID keys from the registry), EnvStatus::detect, Access, and HarnessRuntime; assemble Shared and App (hub capacity 8192, push 1024); bind the weak references; create the bridge socket on unix; spawn files::run_touches and nav::run.
Still in build: for each registry workspace record, skip it if workspace.toml is missing, else app.attach(id, root). Errors are logged only. Then sweep_session_caches.

attach calls WorkspaceRt::open: trust::migrate, trust::seal_file_secrets, WorkspaceDb::open(paths::workspace_db(root)), db.set_workspace_id, host.services(id, root) (yields ServerServices), Engine::new(root, id, db, services), then sync_projects().

attach calls Engine::recover. For each stored session, running executions are finished as Interrupted (or Waiting when an ask is open) with an ExecutionFinished event; open Permission gates are answered Deny by the engine; non-terminal sessions get ensure_driver; finally db.mark_running_interrupted().
attach subscribes to engine.subscribe(), spawns the forwarding task into files, nav, and hub, and stores the runtime in App.workspaces.

Back in run: write server.json (port, url_host, pid), print the sign-in URL, print a network warning when the bind is not loopback, optionally open the browser, then mount api::router(app) and axum::serve with graceful shutdown on ctrl-c. On exit it removes the bridge socket and server.json.
A workspace created while the server runs: the REST handler calls setup::create, which calls ostra_workspace::create::register and then the same app.attach, then registry.mark_onboarded().

patterns.description: Cli has command: Option<Command> and a flattened ServeArgs, so a bare `ostra --port 1` serves. Command::Serve(ServeArgs) repeats the args for the explicit form. main matches each variant; the None arm and the Serve arm both call serve(args). Subcommands that need no server (Config, Url, Sessions, Signout, Stop) call library functions in ostra_server::app or ostra_server::auth and print. Hook and McpStdio call ostra_server::bridge::hook_cli and mcp_cli and exit with their code. Doc comments on variants are the --help text. Adding a command means a new Command variant and a match arm in main.
patterns.name: Clap derive: flattened serve args plus optional subcommand

patterns.description: sessions, signout, and stop do not talk to the server. They call app::open_registry() (owner-only 0600 modes on the db and its -wal and -shm files on unix) and operate on it. stop refuses when auth::server_running() is true (the pid in server.json is alive); otherwise it opens each registered workspace db and calls ostra_engine::runner::stop_session_offline. A running server refuses a revoked sign-in within 5 seconds (RECHECK in auth.rs).
patterns.name: Offline CLI commands open the registry directly

patterns.description: App::attach is the single place a workspace becomes live. It is idempotent: it returns the existing Arc<WorkspaceRt> if the id is open. Otherwise it runs WorkspaceRt::open(shared, id, root), then rt.engine.recover(), then subscribes to engine notices and spawns a task that feeds files.observe, nav.observe, and the hub broadcast (lag is logged and reported to nav.lagged), then inserts the runtime into App.workspaces. Callers are the startup loop in build and setup::create.
patterns.name: Workspace attach: open, recover, forward notices, register

patterns.description: At the end of build, every registry.list_workspaces() record is attached. A workspace whose workspace.toml is missing is skipped with a warning; an attach error is logged with tracing::error and does not stop the server. After the loop, sweep_session_caches removes tool caches of Completed or Failed sessions.
patterns.name: Startup loop over registered workspaces tolerates failures

patterns.description: code_tools, Management, and Coordination are created before App, because the executors need them first, and receive a Weak<App> through bind(&app) afterward.
patterns.name: Late-bound back-references to App

document.problem: Ostra is one binary whose clap definition lives in crates/ostra-server/src/main.rs. The default path (no subcommand) starts the server, which builds shared state, then opens every registered workspace with WorkspaceRt::open, recovers its sessions, and forwards engine notices to a hub. A workspace created at runtime goes through the same App::attach. This document records how both work so a change to startup or to the CLI follows the existing structure.

submit.findings_summary: The whole CLI is one clap-derive tree in crates/ostra-server/src/main.rs, with a flattened ServeArgs so bare `ostra` serves, and subcommands Serve, Hook, McpStdio, Config, Url, Sessions (revoke), Signout and Stop. Offline subcommands call helpers in app.rs and auth.rs and open the registry directly. `serve` calls app::run, which binds, runs app::build (shared state, executors, App), and then attaches every registered workspace through App::attach. attach is idempotent. It calls WorkspaceRt::open (db, Engine::new, sync_projects) and Engine::recover, then forwards engine notices to the hub. Workspaces created at runtime use the same attach through setup::create. Note that crates/ostra-server/src/commands.rs is unrelated to the CLI: it saves project build and test commands.
